newsitem.title: UK: Hungary National Bank seeks $350 mln loan.
newsitem.headline: Hungary National Bank seeks $350 mln loan.

text.p: LONDON, November 15 (LPC) - The National Bank of Hungary (NBH) is seeking a new $350 million syndicated loan, according to a banker close to the deal, joining the growing list of Hungarian borrowers taking advantage of easier terms from international lenders.

Deutsche Bank has the mandate to coordinate arrangers for the loan and is currently in discussions with a group of banks that led a credit for NBH in August. These banks - ABN AMRO Bank, Berliner Bank, Central-European International Bank, Chase Investment Bank, NatWest Markets and Sakura Bank - are all expected to confirm decisions on their involvement shortly.
The new loan will refinance a $350 million loan signed in August. That credit, priced 50 bps over LIBOR, was increased from $250 million after syndication raised $550 million.
Since August loan market conditions for Hungarian borrowers have improved considerably, bankers say, making NBH likely to make substantial savings on the new deal.
Hungary's foreign currency debt rating was raised to BBB minus on October 28 by Standard & Poor's and banks are eager to lend in the country.

By comparison, Hungarian Bank for Investment and Development, which has traditionally been charged more than NBH, is now in the process of raising $60 million at 35 bps over LIBOR, as compared to the 80 bps over LIBOR it was charged in August.
National Bank of Hungary's credit will be launched into general syndication within one or two weeks, the banker said.
